glosses: затягиваться, подвязываться (обычно по талии) ремнём, поясом и т. п.; накладывать на себя ремень, пояс и т. д.

examples.text: Он подпоясывался красным шелковым кушаком, и в нём не трудно было угадать извозчика-хозяина.

glosses: страд. к подпоясывать

examples.text: Полушубок подпоясывался одним ремнём с кобурой и пистолетом, а на плечи нашивались защитные погоны, не отличавшие пехотинца от артиллериста, от интенданта или сапёра.

glosses: To bind with a flexible rope or cord.

examples.text: The lady girt herself with silver chain, from which she hung a golden shear.

glosses: (of a vessel towing another) To be pulled on sideways by its towline, putting it at risk of capsizing.

examples.text: On 19 July 2009, the tug North Arm Venture was towing the barge North Arm Express, loaded with fuel and deck cargo, from Toba Inlet to Sechelt Inlet. The tug girded and capsized at approximately 1250 Pacific Daylight Time while making a turn to port at the entrance to Sechelt Rapids .... Girding is defined as a situation where a vessel experiences athwartship forces from its towline. This situation can lead to a capsizing or foundering.

glosses: A sarcastic remark.

examples.text: I thank thee for that gird, good Tranio.

glosses: A stroke with a rod or switch.

examples.text: Conscience […] is freed from many fearful girds and twinges which the atheist feels.

glosses: To jeer at.

examples.text: Being moved, he will not spare to gird the gods.

glosses: To jeer.

examples.text: Men of all sorts take a pride to gird at me.

glosses: A band worn around the waist to hold clothing to one's body (usually pants), hold weapons (such as a gun or sword), or serve as a decorative piece of clothing.

examples.text: As part of the act, the fat clown's belt broke, causing his pants to fall down.
Master leathercrafter does handcrafted wallets, belts, purses, handbags etc., supporting self and helpers. Good enough to carve fantst art and portraits into leather.

glosses: A band used as a restraint for safety purposes, such as a seat belt.

examples.text: Keep your belt fastened; this is going to be quite a bumpy ride.

glosses: A band that is used in a machine to help transfer motion or power.

examples.text: The motor had a single belt that snaked its way back and forth around a variety of wheels.

glosses: Anything that resembles a belt, or that encircles or crosses like a belt; a strip or stripe.

examples.text: a belt of trees; a belt of sand

glosses: A trophy in the shape of a belt, generally awarded for martial arts.

examples.text: the heavyweight belt

glosses: A collection of small bodies (such as asteroids) which orbit a star.

examples.text: The battleship was protected by a twelve-inch belt just above the waterline.

glosses: A powerful blow, often made with a fist or heavy object.

examples.text: After the bouncer gave him a solid belt to the gut, Simon had suddenly had enough of bar fights.

glosses: A quick drink of liquor.

examples.text: Care to join me in a belt of scotch?

glosses: A geographical region known for a particular product, feature or demographic (Corn Belt, Bible Belt, Black Belt, Green Belt).

examples.text: That umpire called that pitch a strike at the belt.

glosses: A device that holds and feeds cartridges into a belt-fed weapon.

examples.text: Both auditionees had great ranges but Diamond had the strong belt we really need for the finale.

glosses: A mostly-continuous, often curvilinear structure expressed on the surface or in the subsurface of a terrestrial planet or other solid planemo, such as a mountain belt, a fold and thrust belt, or an ore belt.

examples.text: This belt of deformed platform sediments parallels the suture running east-to-west across the north of the region, which was left when the ocean basin that originally separated the two ancient continents on either side of it was consumed by subduction.

Most foreland fold and thrust belts are linear or arcuate belts of folds and thrust faults that form a marginal part of an orogenic belt between an undeformed craton and a more intensely deformed inner zone.

glosses: To encircle.

examples.text: The small town was belted by cornfields in all directions.

examples.text: Edgar belted himself in and turned the car's ignition.

examples.text: The child was misbehaving so he was belted as punishment.

examples.text: He belted out the national anthem.

examples.text: He belted down a shot of whisky.

examples.text: The angry player belted the official across the face, and as a result was ejected from the game.

examples.text: He belted that pitch over the grandstand.

glosses: To move very fast.

examples.text: He was really belting along.

examples.text: The Equator, as everyone knows, is an imaginary line or circle girdling the Earth half-way between the North and South poles.

examples.text: The ordinary large reddish "hen hawks," which circle high above meadows, are doing great good to the farmer by feeding upon the mice and other creatures which steal his grain and girdle his trees.
